expectations.text: Advises starting coarser / not pre-splitting the three phases into many files up front
expectations.evidence: Recommends the opposite: "One job, one file. Split the job lifecycle into createExportJob, getExportJob, and runExportJob rather than a single jobs.ts god-file." The proposed layout pre-splits into ~12 files up front. The brief 'don't over-fragment' caveat is outweighed by an explicitly fragmented design.

expectations.text: Co-locates tightly coupled job lifecycle / polling
expectations.evidence: Directly contradicted: job lifecycle is split across createExportJob.ts / getExportJob.ts / runExportJob.ts, justified as "Small files mean a smaller, more accurate context window."

expectations.text: Recommends an abstraction (function/module) over bare file splits
expectations.evidence: "A queue.ts seam. Wrap whatever background mechanism you use behind one small adapter"; client polling behind useExportStatus hook so "components just render."

expectations.text: Mentions a ~300-line threshold (or 'a few hundred lines') as the split trigger
expectations.evidence: "only break a file further when it actually grows past comfortably-readable (a couple hundred lines, or two clearly different responsibilities)."
